blocks.value: Static variables and methods belong to the class as a whole, not to any individual object. A static variable is shared by every object of its class — change it through one object, and every other object sees the new value too.
Non-constant static variables should normally be private, with access controlled through accessor and mutator methods — the same information-hiding principle as instance variables.
A static method is called on the class name itself, not on an object:
inches = UnitConverter.convertFeetToInches(2.6); // UnitConverter is the class, convertFeetToInches is the static method
Because a static method isn't tied to any particular object, it can't directly reference an instance variable or call a non-static method — unless it creates or is given an object to call it through.

The Math class (already covered in the Predefined Functions module) is a common example of a class made almost entirely of static methods — no import needed, no object needed, just Math.methodName(). One method worth adding to what you've already seen: Math.random() takes no arguments and returns a random double from 0.0 (inclusive) up to but not including 1.0.
